summary: Herrodon, the woodland crown: a queen among her houses, the boundary groves quarrel with Andos Enda, the lost kin of the west and the dragons over the groves.

queens_peace.name: The Queen's Peace
queens_peace.desc: No feud enters the court, and no blade is bared beneath the boughs.

crown_above.name: A Crown Above the Houses
crown_above.desc: The Queen's word ends disputes quickly and the court speaks with one voice.

crown_among.name: A Crown Among the Houses
crown_among.desc: The Queen sits as the first of equals; the houses are loyal because they are heard.

queens_host.name: The Queen's Host
queens_host.desc: The wardens muster in green and gold, and drill as one company.

wall_trade.name: Customs at the Wall
wall_trade.desc: The Wall's toll-keepers are courted, and the merchants of Herrodon pass easily.

groves_defended.name: The Groves Defended
groves_defended.desc: Every tree is a wall and every elder a sentry.

the_queens_court.title: The Queen's Court
the_queens_court.desc: The houses assemble beneath the great boughs for the first court of the Queen's year. The only question is whether they will kneel, as their grandmothers did, or sit.

markers_in_the_groves.title: Markers in the Groves
markers_in_the_groves.desc: Herrodon's foresters find fresh markers set among the boundary groves, in a hand not their own. They ask the Queen whether to set markers of their own beside them, or to leave the trees to grow.

options.name: Leave the groves to the trees.

herrodon_asks_judgement.title: Herrodon Asks for Judgement
herrodon_asks_judgement.desc: A herald from Herrodon stands before the elders of the Magical Forest and asks that they judge the quarrel of the boundary groves, as they judged quarrels before there were crowns. The elders look at one another in silence.

groves_shared.title: The Groves Shared
groves_shared.desc: A herald of Herrodon brings Andos Enda an offer that no one expected: that the boundary groves be held in common, tended by both and claimed by neither. The Speaker and the grove-speakers must decide whether the old quarrel is worth keeping.

under_one_crown.title: Under One Crown
under_one_crown.desc: The Queen of Herrodon has offered her lost kin a place beneath her crown, as subject realms under her protection. The elders of the small realm listen to the herald, and remember how long they have sung Herrodon's songs without wearing its crown.

an_answer_in_the_groves.title: An Answer in the Groves
an_answer_in_the_groves.desc: A rider from [FROM.GetName] reaches the Queen's court with an answer, and the groves have heard it before the Queen has. Herrodon reads it twice and sets it among the court rolls.

focuses.name: The Woodland Crown
focuses.desc: Long ago the houses of the western groves chose a queen, and kept choosing her line. Herrowyn holds court beneath the great boughs, and the houses come to her because they wish to.

focuses.name: Herrowyn's Court
focuses.desc: The Queen's court is a living hall of arching trees. Heralds, wardens and elders come and go beneath the boughs, and the Queen hears each of them in turn.

focuses.name: The Crowned Houses
focuses.desc: Each great house has a seat beneath the Queen's own, and a voice in her council. The crown may be hers, but the council is theirs.

focuses.name: The Queen's Peace
focuses.desc: Queen Herrowyn lays down her peace over the groves: no feud may be carried into the court, and no blade may be bared beneath the boughs.

focuses.name: A Crown Above the Houses
focuses.desc: The Queen's word is made the final one in all disputes between the houses. Quarrels are shorter, though a few elders remember when the houses would have argued longer.

focuses.name: A Crown Among the Houses
focuses.desc: The Queen sits as the first of equals, and the houses decide with her, not under her. The crown wins a deeper loyalty and gives up a measure of command.

focuses.name: The Crown of Herrodon
focuses.desc: The crown of leaves and old gold is lifted from its cedar chest and worn for the first time in a generation. Herrodon is a realm, and it wishes to be seen as one.

focuses.name: The Boundary Groves
focuses.desc: Between Herrodon and its eastern neighbour stands a stretch of groves that both realms claim, and neither will name. Herrodon's oldest quarrel grows there, one root at a time.

focuses.name: Honour the Old Slights
focuses.desc: The houses recite the grievances against Andos Enda, one by one, in the old order. Every slight is remembered, and none is yet avenged.

focuses.name: Let the Groves Grow Wild
focuses.desc: The Queen declares that no marker shall be set among the boundary groves and no axe lifted. If the trees may have them, neither realm can.

focuses.name: Markers of Stone
focuses.desc: Cairns of grey stone and a small watch-post mark the Queen's claim in the boundary groves. Her neighbours look on with narrowed eyes.

focuses.name: Ask the Forest to Judge
focuses.desc: The Queen sends a message to the Magical Forest, whose elders have judged between elves since before there was a crown to quarrel over, and asks that they say whose the groves are.

focuses.name: The Feud of the Groves
focuses.desc: Patience is spent. Herrodon lays a claim on the nearest of Andos Enda's groves and takes up the old quarrel in earnest, though the elders pray it will stay a quarrel of one state.

focuses.name: The Groves Shared
focuses.desc: With the quarrel cooled, Herrodon proposes to Andos Enda that the boundary groves be held in common, tended by both and owned by none.

focuses.name: Songs of the Western Groves
focuses.desc: Herrodon's singers walk west to the small realms that sing its songs without wearing its crown, and sing them again where they were first learned.

focuses.name: A Kin-Bond with Sacomananos
focuses.desc: The Queen sends a ring of green gold to Sacomananos and a promise that Herrodon's hand will never be raised against its lost kin.

focuses.name: A Kin-Bond with Velakton
focuses.desc: The same ring, in silver, goes to Velakton, with the same promise and the same hope that the kin will answer it.

focuses.name: One Crown of the Woods
focuses.desc: The Queen offers her lost kin a place beneath one crown. They may take it as subject realms with Herrodon's protection, or keep their own songs and their own borders.

focuses.name: Wings at Dusk
focuses.desc: At dusk a wide shadow crosses the western groves, and the herders lower their eyes. The Queen has the seasons' offerings set out on the high ridge.

focuses.name: Gifts to the Keeper
focuses.desc: Herrodon sends gifts to the Keeper of the dragons: honey, silver and a wreath of the oldest boughs. Whoever keeps Dragon Mountain is a friend worth the cost.

focuses.name: Roost Songs
focuses.desc: The oldest songs of the groves are sung at the foot of Dragon Mountain, in the tongue the wyrms are said to prefer. The roosts are quiet, and the singers are not unwelcome.

focuses.name: A Wing for Herrodon
focuses.desc: In the hour of need the Keeper sends a dragon to the groves. It will fight for Herrodon as long as the Queen holds faith with the roost, and the cost is not small.

focuses.name: The Queen's Wardens
focuses.desc: The Queen's wardens wear green and bear her sigil on their quivers. They are taught by the oldest foresters, who tell them the groves are the true armour of Herrodon.

focuses.name: Bows of Herrodon
focuses.desc: Herrodon's bowyers cut the long yew of the western groves. A Herrodon bow has a pale limb and a dark one, and the pair is never separated.

focuses.name: Grove Knights
focuses.desc: Mounted wardens ride the grove lanes in the Queen's livery, carrying lances of ash and bright pennons. They are for show as much as for war, and not only for show.

focuses.name: The Queen's Host
focuses.desc: On the great feast days the Queen's wardens muster beneath her banner. It is a spectacle, and a promise to everyone who sees it.

focuses.name: Kin of Herrodon
focuses.desc: Herrodon sends its heralds to the Magical Forest with songs and gifts, and asks that the old forest remember it as kin, not as a rival.

focuses.name: Stand with the Kindred
focuses.desc: The Kindred of the Woods stands, and the Queen puts her name to it. Herrodon will defend elven land, but will not march beyond it, and will not stand beside men.

focuses.name: Healers of Herrodon
focuses.desc: The Queen's healers go out in grey cloaks, not green, so that none may say Herrodon has sent a host. They carry herbs, bandages and few words.

focuses.name: Customs at the Wall
focuses.desc: Herrodon's factors treat the Great Wall's toll-keepers as honoured guests and settle every old complaint at the gate, with a smile and a purse.

focuses.name: The Groves Defended
focuses.desc: The first stranger's boot has touched the western groves. The horns of Herrodon sound under the boughs, and every house sends its strong to the Queen.

focuses.name: The Queen Rides
focuses.desc: Herrowyn herself rides at the head of her wardens, in a mantle of green and gold. The sight is worth a thousand bows.

focuses.name: The Kin Answer
focuses.desc: Companies of kin come in from the neighbouring groves, with bows strung and food for ten days. No one told them to come.

focuses.name: The Groves Are Quiet
focuses.desc: The enemy is gone and the groves are whole. The Queen lays aside her mantle, and the herders raise their eyes to the sky again.
